presets.title: Baseline PINN warm-up
presets.intent: Stable normalized reference run with no teacher supervision. Use this as the comparison point before adding teacher guidance.
presets.notes: Validated as the reference bundle for later comparisons in the 2026-05-17 offline sweep. Normalization stays on because it was consistently part of every stronger run.

presets.title: Base Frame Load-Patch + Boundary Guidance
presets.intent: Use this when the current geometry is the base frame and the plain PINN is under-predicting stress near the top patch.
presets.notes: Confirmed as the best base-frame recipe in the 2026-05-17 confirmation sweep. Load-patch-only guidance was worse, so keep some boundary anchors with the load-patch teachers.

presets.title: Braced Frame Interior-Heavy Guidance
presets.intent: Start here for diagonal or x-brace geometries when the PINN misses reinforcement-region stress and needs stronger bulk guidance.
presets.notes: Confirmed as the best diagonal-frame recipe in the 2026-05-17 confirmation sweep. Use this as the first reinforced-geometry preset before escalating to adaptive sampling.

presets.title: Adaptive Reinforced-Frame Follow-Up
presets.intent: Escalate from the interior-heavy preset when a reinforced frame still misses brace stress, especially on x-brace cases.
presets.notes: Confirmed as the best x-brace recipe in the 2026-05-17 confirmation sweep. Adaptive sampling helped this reinforced case more than it helped the diagonal or base frame.

presets.title: Adaptive collocation
presets.intent: Use this as a secondary follow-up when teacher-guided training plateaus and you want the collocation cloud to move toward the high-error regions.
presets.notes: Helpful as a follow-up toggle, not as a universal first intervention. In the 2026-05-17 sweep it helped the x-brace case more than the base frame, and it did not beat the strongest non-adaptive base recipe.

presets.title: Refine the FEM mesh
presets.intent: Reduce discretization error in the structured FEM baseline.
presets.notes: Doubling cells per side roughly quarters interpolation error in smooth regions, at higher solve cost.
